summary.en: Israel is conducting air, drone and ground operations in southern Lebanon, striking targets and carrying out detonations that have killed civilians and injured others, while Hezbollah fires artillery at Israeli positions and has begun cash payments to war victims and displaced families. The United Nations reports 300,000 people displaced in Lebanon by the fighting. Israel has also built a new road in the Shebaa Valley buffer zone, a development not mentioned previously. The conflict, which began in October 2023, continues to generate civilian hardship and displacement. 4,335 battle-related deaths occurred in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Israel gjennomfører luft-, drone- og bakkoperasjoner i Sør-Libanon, slår mål og utfører detonasjoner som har drept sivile og såret andre, mens Hizbollah skyter artilleri mot israelske posisjoner og har begynt med kontantutbetalinger til krigsofre og fordrevne familier. FN rapporterer at 300 000 personer er fordrevet i Libanon på grunn av kampene. Israel har også bygget en ny vei i bufferområdet Shebaa-dalen, en utvikling som ikke ble nevnt tidligere. Konflikten, som startet i oktober 2023, fortsetter å påføre sivile vanskeligheter og fordrivelse. 4 335 dødsfall knyttet til kamper fant sted i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)
background.extract: An ongoing conflict between the Lebanese militant group Hezbollah and Israel began on 8 October 2023, when Hezbollah launched rockets and artillery at Israeli positions following Hamas's October 7 attacks on Israel. The conflict escalated into a prolonged exchange of bombardments, leading to extensive displacement in Israel and Lebanon. The conflict is part of the broader Middle Eastern crisis that began with Hamas's attack, with the short Israeli invasion of Lebanon in 2024 marking the largest escalation of the Hezbollah–Israel conflict since the 2006 Lebanon War. In Arabic, the conflict (2023–2024) is referred to as the "Support War" or the "Gaza Support War."
